title: Motion in straight line

answer.content: **Instantaneous velocity** is the velocity of an object at a specific, infinitely small instant of time. Mathematically, it is the limit of the average velocity as the time interval approaches zero (the derivative of position with respect to time: dx/dt).

explanation: This introduces calculus concepts into the understanding of motion.

title: Motion in plane
ques: When an object moves in a circular path with constant speed, why is its motion considered **accelerated**?

answer.content:
Even though the speed (magnitude) is constant, the **direction** of the velocity vector is continuously changing at every point along the circular path.

Since velocity is a vector (magnitude + direction), a change in direction means the velocity is changing, which by definition means the object is accelerating (centripetal acceleration).

explanation: This tests the understanding of vectors in two-dimensional motion.

title: Relative velocity
ques: Train A is moving East at 50 km/h, and Train B is moving West at 60 km/h on parallel tracks. What is the **relative velocity of Train A with respect to Train B**?

answer.content:
Since they are moving in opposite directions, we add their magnitudes to find the relative speed.

Relative velocity = Velocity of A - Velocity of B
Assuming East is positive (+50) and West is negative (-60):
Relative velocity = 50 - (-60) = **110 km/h towards East**.

explanation: This applies vector addition/subtraction to real-world scenarios from different frames of reference.

title: Projectile motion
ques: For a given initial velocity, at what **angle of projection** is the horizontal range of a projectile maximum?

answer.content: The horizontal range is maximum when the angle of projection is **45 degrees**.

explanation: This is a classic optimization problem in kinematics.
